correctness.rationale: The nonzero Jacobian locus is exactly |z|^2=kc/(k+2). Its image has imaginary part proportional to -2 sin^3(theta) U_k'(cos theta). The real part at every stationary angle is 2U_k(cos theta)/k, including the endpoints by direct substitution. For odd k, interlaced simple Chebyshev zeros and the exact identity |U_k(x)|=[1-k(k+2)x^2/(k+1)^2]^{-1/2} make all (k+1)/2 positive heights distinct. This gives both directions of the critical-coefficient characterization; Brilleslyper et al., Theorem 1.1, independently establishes the total number and zero-count jumps. At the central extrema h_min=1+O(k^-2), giving width 2 log(k)/k with the claimed remainder. The supplied SymPy check.py was executed successfully (164 diagnostics); finite tests are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The June 2020 primary paper gives the number and ordered jumps but only c_1 explicitly and a bound for c_N; its Section 3 question 2 calls for exact interior coefficients. The present gap-two Chebyshev-extremum formula determines every coefficient, including the last, and proves a sharp logarithmic width. Indexed related results treat other exponent or parameter problems, not this coefficient list. This is a best-knowledge, not an absolute, priority assessment.
residual_risks: Independent historical priority assessment has not been performed.
The full texts of a potentially relevant 2022 location article and a 2025 complex-parameter article were unavailable; an equivalent derivation could exist there.
Two adjacent publicly indexed mathematical results were checked by returned scientific summaries rather than primary full text because their public pages were inaccessible.

The 2020 paper gives an implicit crossing mechanism, so the exact formula may be derivable by a different published trigonometric reduction; the distinctive sharp large-degree width mitigates, but does not eliminate, priority uncertainty.

value.rationale: The exponent gap n-k=2 is a canonical infinite coprime harmonic-trinomial family, and exact locations of zero-count transitions were posed as an explicit problem by the main motivating paper. The new formula covers every transition in every odd degree, computes the previously bounded last coefficient even for the elementary n=5 example, and gives the sharp nontrivial (2 log k)/k collapse of the entire phase-transition window. These invariant parameter values are motivated by bifurcation geometry and may guide parameter studies; they are not arbitrary slices or simply numerical confirmations of published counts.
